outputs.exact_statement: The electronic promise problem for [eq:electronic-H] on $\mathcal H_N$, with distinct rational nuclear positions, all nuclear charges equal to one, unary electron number, and rational thresholds separated by at least $L^{-1}$, is QMA-hard under deterministic classical polynomial-time many-one reductions. The reduction produces polynomially many nuclei and electrons, polynomial rational bit lengths, and threshold separation at least one. The only output data are the nuclear positions, electron number, and thresholds.

Let $A,B$ be self-adjoint operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space. Suppose $A$ has kernel projection $P\ne0$, $A\ge gQ$, where $Q=I-P$ and $g>0$, and $\|B\|\le g/4$. Then $$E(A+B)=E\big((PBP-PBA^{-1}BP)|_P\big)+O(\|B\|^3/g^2)$$ where the inverse vanishes on the kernel.

For the density and separated centers constructed above, with the polynomial scale chosen sufficiently large, there are fixed constants $c>0,C<\infty$ such that $$\begin{split}
 (I-P)L_c(I-P)&\ge c(I-P)\quad\text{on the complement},\\
 L_c&\ge -\Delta_y/2-C,\qquad
 \|L_cP\|\le p(n,D)\lambda^{-0.9}.
 \end{split}                                                       \tag{6}\label{eq:6}$$ The inequalities are quadratic-form inequalities on the one-particle $H^1$ domain, and the last bound is an operator norm from the range of $P$ to $L^2$. All estimates hold with either spin included.

For the unit-nucleus construction above with $N=m$, and sufficiently large polynomial scale $\lambda$, the full antisymmetric $m$-electron operator in dilated and shifted units satisfies $$E_\Pi-p(n,D)\lambda^{-4/3}
                   \ \le\ \inf\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal H\ \le\ E_\Pi.       \tag{8}\label{eq:8}$$ The lower bound holds on every normalized antisymmetric $H^1$ state, including every spin sector.

For the constructed unit nuclei with $N=m$, let $\mathcal H$ be the dilated and shifted continuum operator above and let $H_d$ be the finite fermion Hamiltonian [eq:2]. At sufficiently large polynomial scale, $$|\lambda\inf\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal H-E(H_d)| \le p(n,D)\lambda^{-0.1}. \tag{9}\label{eq:9}$$
